title: A conforming contract surface
description: Every numeric position here is one this checker is content with, and the file exists so the red proof has a control: a checker that refused everything would satisfy every breakage below it, so none of them means anything without this coming back green — and green AND WARNING-FREE, because a control that arrives already complaining cannot tell a conforming surface from one the checker has an opinion about. Every breakage in numeric_self_test.sh edits exactly ONE field of this file, which is what lets each red name the position it fired about.

id.description: An identifier, and a string for the reason the whole rule exists: a UUID a client may hold is exact in every one of the six languages, including the one that rounds everything through float64.

quantity.description: A bounded count. The maximum is declared and it is below the float64 exact range, so no reader can be handed a value it cannot hold.

version.description: A small non-negative integer with a ceiling well under 2**53. The breakages below rename this field and retype it; the ceiling is what makes it safe here.

status.description: A CLOSED SET OF WORDS, not a numeric enum. Codegen turns this into a union of strings and adding one is still a breaking change — but it is a breaking change a client can survive, and it is the spelling the reference's own convention implies.

retry_count.description: An UNBOUNDED unsigned integer whose name says nothing about identity. This is the fleet's own vocabulary — counts, amounts in minor units, status codes — and it is green here on purpose: `numeric.unsigned` is in the notEnforced ledger, and this field is the surface it would have fired on.

payload.description: An opaque envelope. A union that merely PERMITS number among six types is not a float field, and refusing it would refuse every opaque payload in the fleet.
